input: nums has at most 20000 nonnegative integers, each at most 20000, and total sum at most 20000. Integers l,r satisfy 0 <= l <= r <= 20000. Empty nums is an accepted extension. Collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse/accessor-backed collections. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. Every collection length and computed allocation size fits [0,4294967295], with padded sizes explicitly included. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is allowed. Preconditions are not runtime-checked, and allocation/resource capacity or completion is not guaranteed by declared bounds. Python integer inputs are plain int, excluding bool.
return: Number of distinct sub-multisets with sum in [l,r], modulo 1000000007. Equal-valued occurrences are indistinguishable; selecting different zero multiplicities gives distinct multisets. The empty multiset has sum zero.
mutation_aliasing: Inputs and caller-held aliases remain unchanged; working state is private. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Zero choices initialize counts[0] to zeroMultiplicity+1. For positive v with count c, following[s]=counts[s]+following[s-v]-counts[s-(c+1)*v], omitting out-of-range terms, enforces multiplicity bounds. Adding M before remainder handles negative intermediate values consistently. All arithmetic is below 3M, and excluded indices are at most 40000. All integer inputs/intermediates remain within [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: Expected O(n+D*(r+1)+r+1) time and O(D+r+1) live auxiliary space for D distinct positive values, including frequency map and a constant number of DP rows. Each distinct multiplicity is processed once, not each labeled subset. Bounds include ordinary built-in operations/allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop and any explicitly stated hash/sort behavior.
source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 1002 UTF-8 bytes, including every helper, Solution wrapper, signature, loop, built-in call, annotation/comment, whitespace and terminal newline. Helpers are fully charged per candidate, not free shared libraries. No imports, runtime-generated implementations or hidden source expansion are used. Any eventual judge-interface adapter is additional charged source.
